entities.summary: Titus Romilius Rocus Vaticanus, a Roman politician, played a significant role in shaping the early Roman Republic. As consul in 455 BC and decemvir in 451 BC, he contributed to the creation of the Roman Constitution. His legacy can be seen in the subsequent development of Roman law and governance. The decline of the Roman Republic in the 1st century BC was, in part, a response to the corruption and instability brought about by Rocus Vaticanus's actions. His fate, sealed by the Roman Senate, serves as a reminder of the fragility of power in ancient Rome.
